prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Labour Party Manifesto 2024 — Summary (under 500 words)

Core purpose
- Change built on service, security and stability after 14 years of Conservative “chaos.”
- Mission‑driven government with five long‑term missions:
  1) Highest sustained growth in the G7
  2) Clean power by 2030
  3) Halve serious violent crime and restore confidence in policing
  4) Break down barriers to opportunity (childcare, schools, skills)
  5) Build an NHS fit for the future

Foundations and fiscal rules
- Strong national security, secure borders, economic stability.
- Fiscal rules: balance day‑to‑day budget; debt falling by year 5. One major fiscal event a year; OBR oversight. No rises in National Insurance, Income Tax rates or VAT. Tackle avoidance: abolish non‑dom status; close private equity “carried interest” loophole; modernise HMRC.

Economy and growth
- Pro‑business, pro‑worker “securonomics” with a strategic state.
- Industrial Strategy and statutory Industrial Strategy Council; boost innovation (AI, data, R&D 10‑year budgets).
- National Wealth Fund (£7.3bn) to crowd in private capital: ports, gigafactories, steel, CCS, hydrogen.
- Planning reform to build 1.5m homes; brownfield first, strategic “grey belt” releases; new towns; stronger social/affordable housing; permanent mortgage guarantee.
- Replace business rates in England; cap corporation tax at 25%; permanent full expensing.
- Infrastructure: 10‑year strategy; new National Infrastructure and Service Transformation Authority; gigabit and 5G by 2030.
- Transport: bring rail into public ownership as contracts end; empower mayors on integrated transport; EV charging rollout; fix 1m potholes/yr.
- Devolution: new Local Growth Plans; multi‑year council funding.
- Immigration: reduce net migration; link visas to skills plans; tougher enforcement on abuses.
- Work: New Deal for Working People—ban exploitative zero‑hours, end fire‑and‑rehire, day‑one rights, Single Enforcement Body; minimum wage reflects cost of living; end age bands.
- Employment support: youth guarantee (training/apprenticeship/help to work) for 18–21s.

Clean energy and environment
- Clean power by 2030: double onshore wind, triple solar, quadruple offshore wind; invest in CCS, hydrogen, marine; new nuclear (Sizewell C, SMRs); maintain strategic gas reserve; no new North Sea exploration licences (manage existing fields).
- Great British Energy (£8.3bn) to co‑invest and back local power; upgrade grid; tougher regulator and fairer standing charges.
- Warm Homes Plan: £6.6bn to upgrade 5m homes.
- Nature: expand habitats; three new National Forests; crack down on sewage—special measures for water firms, tough fines and bonus bans.
- Support British farming; phase out badger cull; stronger animal welfare (ban trail hunting, trophy imports, puppy smuggling, snares).

Crime and justice
- Neighbourhood Policing Guarantee: thousands more officers/PCSOs; Respect Orders to curb antisocial behaviour; specific offence for assaults on shopworkers.
- Knife crime plan: mandatory interventions; ban zombie/machete‑style knives; accountability for online sales; Young Futures hubs nationwide.
- Halve violence against women and girls: rape units in every force; fast‑track courts; stronger stalking and spiking laws; raise police standards; prisons expansion and reoffending reduction; Hillsborough Law; Windrush Commissioner.

Opportunity, childcare, schools and skills
- 3,000 new primary‑based nurseries; free primary school breakfast clubs; 6,500 new teachers; curriculum and assessment reform; SEND inclusion; mental health professionals in every school.
- Skills England; reform Apprenticeship Levy to a flexible Growth and Skills Levy; Technical Excellence Colleges; secure future for higher education.

NHS and social care
- Cut waits: 40,000 extra weekly appointments (evenings/weekends); shared waiting lists; use spare independent capacity.
- Double CT/MRI scanners; deliver New Hospitals Programme; modernise NHS app and procurement/innovation.
- Return of the family doctor; more GPs; community pharmacist prescribing; neighbourhood health centres.
- Dentistry Rescue Plan: 700,000 urgent appointments; contract reform; supervised tooth‑brushing for 3–5s.
- National Care Service with national standards; Fair Pay Agreement in adult social care.
- 8,500 extra mental health staff; Young Futures hubs; modernise Mental Health Act.
- Public health: smoke‑free generation; restrict child‑targeted vapes/junk‑food ads; energy drink sales to under‑16s banned.

Democracy and the Union
- Independent Ethics and Integrity Commission; modernise Commons; immediate Lords reforms (end hereditary peers; retirement at 80) and consult on replacement second chamber; votes at 16.
- Reset with devolved governments; uphold ECHR.

Foreign, defence and development
- Unshakeable NATO and nuclear deterrent; Strategic Defence Review and path to 2.5% GDP on defence; defence industrial strategy; steadfast support to Ukraine; AUKUS; balanced China approach.
- Make Brexit work: better EU trade (veterinary deal, MRAs), security pact; no return to SM/CU/FoM.
- Trade strategy focused on UK strengths; India FTA priority; modernise global trade rules.
- Lead a Clean Power Alliance; rebuild development leadership; restore 0.7% aid when fiscal conditions allow.

First steps
- Economic stability; 40,000 more NHS appointments a week; Border Security Command; Great British Energy; antisocial behaviour crackdown and youth hubs; 6,500 new teachers.
